title: The Crossing
logline: Where the stream has no bridge, people cross by a rope tied to a tree: a run-up, a grip, a swing, an unsteady landing, and then, every time, a moment of standing firm on the far side.
human_question: Is the moment you let go of the rope the same moment you are safe, or are those two different things?

premise.story: A village where a stream or channel with no bridge is crossed daily by rope, log or pole, followed through a season, in calm weather and in flood.
premise.place: A hill-country or wet-zone village where a stream separates homes from fields, a school path, or a market road.
premise.experience: The small, repeated physical drama of committing to a crossing: the grip, the release, the unsteady first step, the recovery.

concept_links.why: Both sources describe the decisive moment of path and fruition with a canal-crossing simile: a man runs, grips a rope, swings, lets go, and lands shaking before he finds his footing; recognising and letting go are treated as two different moments, only the second of which actually crosses [C100-P4:L44–L46].
What changes at such a crossing, in the source's account, does not come back; the film's crossings are ordinary and repeatable, an honest, non-equivalent echo of that idea.

what_camera_could_observe: The run-up, the grip on the rope or log, the swing or step across
The unsteady first second on the far bank, then the settled stride
The same crossing made by a child, a farmer carrying produce, an older person who hesitates
The crossing in different water: low and calm, high and fast after rain
what_must_be_real: A crossing people actually rely on, not one staged for the camera. No one is asked to cross dangerously for a better shot.

possible_arc.turn: The same crossing attempted by someone less confident, or in rising water.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the crossings on the day of filming actually look like.

requirements: A real village where a bridgeless crossing is part of daily life
Consent from the community and anyone filmed crossing
Safety oversight; the crew must never encourage a risky crossing

suggestions.name: A hill-country or wet-zone village with a seasonal stream crossing
suggestions.why: Bridgeless stream crossings by rope, log or pole are still part of daily life in some hill-country villages.
suggestions.verify: A specific village and crossing must be identified and confirmed safe to film.

risks: Making a real hardship (no bridge) look picturesque or purely symbolic
Safety of anyone filmed crossing in high water
drop_if: No such crossing can be found and filmed safely, or the community does not want it shown as a hardship

connections.note: The same season's harvest, taken stock of, flows into this idea's image of crossing and letting go.
Both ask whether a change is temporary or complete, one through a crossing, one through a farmer's choice about a weed.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
